newsitem.title: USA: Hilton to purchase remaining Bally's Grand shares.
newsitem.headline: Hilton to purchase remaining Bally's Grand shares.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. Friday said it would acquire the 15 percent of Bally's Grand Inc. it does not already own and merge Bally's Las Vegas resort-casino into Hilton in a deal valued at about $50 million.

The move settles a months-long legal battle between Bally's Grand investors and Hilton. Last November, two major shareholders sued Beverly Hills, Calif.-based Hilton and unit Bally Entertainment, alleging they bought Bally's Grand land on the Las Vegas Strip at below fair market value.

That lawsuit, filed in Delaware Chancery Court by New York-based Tower Investment Group Inc. and Executive Life of New York, was settled by Hilton with the payment of $52.75 a share for all the shares held by the two groups.

Hilton currently owns about 85 percent of Bally's Grand stock. After the settlement is approved in court, it will own nearly 100 percent and merge Bally's Grand into Hilton or into one of its wholly owned units.
The stock repurchase is set to occur on or before June 26. Hilton also will buy back all Bally's Grand common stock purchase warrants.

Hilton acquired Bally Entertainment Inc. last year for about $3.0 billion, including assumption of debt. The acquisition included plans by Bally Entertainment, which then owned the 85 percent stake in Bally's Grand, to build its "Paris" hotel and casino on land next to Bally's Grand.

The shareholders claimed the land, which had been owned by Bally's Grand, was sold to Bally Entertainment last summer at below market value to facilitate the Hilton deal. They said the sale diminished their opportunity to participate in profits from "Paris," which is now under construction.
Hilton and Bally had denied the allegations.
Hilton stock rose 12.5 cents to $28.625 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, while Bally's Grand jumped $11 to $50 on Nasdaq.
